about.narrative: Audivise, version 1, local and private edition. System architected by Eliezer Tavares de Oliveira. This is the continuation of the work started in Integrative Project V (Projeto Integrador V), of the Computer Engineering course at UNIVESP. It is now a personal, non-academic project. This edition runs entirely on your device: the decision engine is written in Rust, compiled to WebAssembly, and face detection is local. No image, coordinate or word ever leaves your machine.

voiceInstall.title: No voice found on this system
voiceInstall.intro: There is no installed voice for {language}. To hear the guidance in this language, install a system voice — this needs to be done only once:
voiceInstall.windows: Windows: Settings → Time & Language → Speech → Manage voices → Add voices → choose {language}.
voiceInstall.macos: macOS: System Settings → Accessibility → Spoken Content → System Voice → Manage Voices → download a {language} voice.
voiceInstall.android: Android: Settings → System → Languages & input → Output → Text-to-speech → Google Text-to-Speech → Install voice data → {language}.
voiceInstall.ios: iPhone/iPad: Settings → Accessibility → Spoken Content → Voices → add a voice for {language}.
voiceInstall.linux: Linux: install speech-dispatcher with a voice for {language} (for example, espeak-ng or RHVoice), or use Google Chrome, which ships its own voices.
voiceInstall.chrome: Chrome: Google voices are usually built in; make sure the browser is up to date and tap Check again.
voiceInstall.once: This notice appears only once per language. Audivise still works without a voice: every guidance is also shown as text.
